messages:
Maya R: Quick sync — I pushed a draft of a 1-page "security + SLA" brief aimed at CTOs and platform leads. Objective: one deck for sales + a short webpage snippet we can use for the webinar landing page. Need final copy + product accuracy checks by EOD Friday. Link: https://drive.redwood/example/cto-brief :eyes:
Jonah P: skimmed it, looks tight. A couple of product notes: include explicit line about Dedicated capacity latency SLOs and fallback routing to lower-cost variants. Suggest a small table for deploy modes (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) with a one-line recommended buyer scenario each.
Priya S: please add KMS/HSM integration and SOC2 mention under "Security controls". Also an explicit note about customer-managed keys for Private deployments — that matters for regulated buyers.
Maya R: good call, Priya. Jonah — can you draft the tiny table? Ana — can you write the 3-line tech blurb on how routing/fallback works (high level, non-technical) for the exec audience?
Ana K: will do. Also suggest a 2-line "what to expect" under SLAs: uptime commitment + typical P90 latency for text gen. Keep numbers conservative.
Luke G: sales ask — include a short inbound routing snippet: when a lead says "on-prem requirement" route to AE + solutions-engineering; if they mention "SLA cert" route to enterprise-sales. Can we add a 1-click field in the form? :+1:
Maya R: yes. I'll update the lead form copy: add checkbox "Requires Private/VPC or KMS" and radio for SLA tier. Ops-bot, can you create a short landing URL and add UTM for the webinar?
ops-bot: Created landing page https://redwood.ai/cto-brief-2026?utm_source=slack&utm_campaign=cto_brief and short link https://rwd.ai/cto-brief-26.
Jonah P: For the webinar narrative, let's highlight a 3-part sequence: 1) security & control, 2) predictable economics (Dedicated + Optimize), 3) rollout story + migration checklist. Each part should have one slide and one customer snippet.
Priya S: for compliance slide add bullets: SOC2, ISO27701 (in progress), customer-managed keys, audit logs retention options. Keep legal phrasing minimal — "supports" rather than "compliant" unless legal confirms.
Ana K: drafting the 3-line tech blurbs now. I'll add a tiny checklist called "CTO quick decision guide" — 4 bullets: data residency? SLA needs? Integration time? who's owning infra?
Luke G: can marketing also create a 1-paragraph battlecard for AEs that reads like: pain > why Redwood > how we mitigate > ask (next step)? Need this by Monday morning for the field.
Maya R: yes — I can have the battlecard and the one-pager final by Monday AM. Jonah/Priya/Ana please drop your one-line inputs in the doc by end of day Friday. Luke — I'll include the inbound-routing copy and AE battlecard in the same folder.
Maya R: final editorial asks: shorten the headline to "Secure inference with predictable SLAs" and subhead: "Choose Hosted, Dedicated, or Private — same API, different controls." Thoughts? :thinking_face:
Jonah P: headline sounds good. Maybe change to "Secure, predictable inference" to flip the emphasis to security+predictability. Either works.
Priya S: both concise. prefer "Secure, predictable inference".
Luke G: prefer the shorter one for email subject lines.
Maya R: ok locking "Secure, predictable inference". I'll iterate the doc and ping when ready. Thanks everyone :pray:
